transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… yeah, thanks for seeing me. I guess the main thing is work. I’m a nurse, and on the floor I keep losing my train of thought constantly. Like I’ll be in the middle of sorting out a patient flow issue, and then an IV pump beeps, or someone asks another nurse a question nearby, or a call light goes off, and suddenly it’s just… gone. I can’t remember what I was doing.

And I know hospitals are noisy, that’s normal—honestly sometimes I think about how nobody who designs those alarms has ever had to listen to them for twelve hours—but it’s gotten to where I’m really worried about how often I get pulled off track.
Before this got worse at work, have you had trouble staying focused and getting distracted easily since childhood?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, it’s hard because when you’re a kid you don’t really think of it as “focus,” you just think you’re in trouble again. But even in elementary school, my teachers would write things like I was bright but careless, or that I lost worksheets all the time, or forgot to turn in homework.

My mom used to have to sit with me every night to keep me on track, which I hated at the time because I wanted to be done and go do literally anything else. And then I’d get distracted by, like, sharpening a pencil or reorganizing my backpack instead of actually finishing the assignment. So… yeah, it was definitely there before work got bad.
Do you get similarly distracted in other parts of your life outside of work?

Yeah, I do, but work is where it feels the scariest, I guess, because there are consequences. Like on the floor I’ll be trying to manage a patient flow thing, and then an IV pump starts beeping, or someone nearby asks a question, or a call light goes off, and it’s like my brain just drops the thread completely.

Outside of work it’s similar in the sense that little things can pull me away, but the hospital makes it really obvious because there’s always something interrupting you. It’s not like, “Oh, I got briefly distracted,” it’s more like I have to stop and reconstruct what I was even doing. Which is exhausting.
Have these concentration problems gotten noticeably worse recently compared with how you’ve usually been?

Yeah, noticeably worse… or maybe more noticeable. It became a major problem when I took on the expanded charge-nurse responsibilities, which was almost two years ago now.

Before that I was always kind of scattered, but once I had more of that role—keeping track of all these moving pieces—it was like the cracks got really obvious. And I remember thinking at first, “Well, everyone feels overwhelmed in charge,” because that’s what people say, and also hospitals love to pretend chaos is a personality test, but… no, it’s been pretty consistently bad since then.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an immediate problem in front of you?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, I do think about things a lot, but I don’t know if I’d call it worrying exactly. Sometimes I’m just replaying stuff or trying to remember what I was supposed to do, and then I end up thinking about some completely different thing, like whether I paid a bill or if I left something in my car.

But “worrying even when there isn’t a problem”… I don’t know. I guess I’d need you to say what you mean by worrying, because my brain is kind of always doing something, but I’m not sure it’s that.
Do you often find yourself unable to stop or control your worrying?

I don’t know if I’d say I’m unable to stop worrying. Like, I get stuck thinking about things, but it’s hard for me to tell if that’s worry or just my brain jumping around and not letting me finish one thought before it grabs another one.

Sometimes I’ll try to answer that question and then I’m thinking about whether I texted someone back, or if I forgot something I meant to bring in from the car, and then I’m annoyed because that’s not even what we were talking about. So… I’m not sure. I don’t have a clean yes or no for that.
Outside of work, have these attention problems caused significant problems in your daily life?

Yeah. I mean, it’s not just work. At home it’s embarrassing, honestly. I forget things that should be automatic, like calling my sister back, or paying a bill, or I’ll have an appointment and I swear I knew about it, I put it in my phone, and then somehow I still miss it or remember too late.

And it’s weird because I’ll fully mean to do the thing—like, “Okay, after I make coffee I’m going to call,” and then I notice the dishwasher needs unloading, and then I’m looking for a charger, and then two days later I’m like, oh my God, I never called. Same with reminders sometimes. They go off and I’ll think, “Okay, in one second,” and then it’s just gone. So yeah, it causes real problems outside of work too.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?

I don’t think so? I mean, I have days where I feel really frustrated with myself, like when I realize I forgot something again, and then I kind of beat myself up about it for a while. But depressed most days… I’m not sure I’d describe it that way.

I guess I’d have to think about what counts as depressed. Like, tired and irritated and overwhelmed sometimes, yes, but “down most days” doesn’t immediately feel like the right word.
Do you often feel restless, like you have trouble sitting still?

Restless like… physically? I’m not sure. I don’t think of myself as someone who’s bouncing off the walls or anything. I can sit if I have to, especially if I’m with a patient or in a situation where I know I’m supposed to be still.

But then again, I do move around a lot at home, like I’ll get up to get water and then I’m suddenly wiping the counter or checking something in another room, but I don’t know if that’s restlessness or just me getting sidetracked. Sorry, I’m not answering that very clearly. I guess I haven’t really noticed it as a main problem.
Have you had any medical or neurological problem—like a head injury, seizures, thyroid trouble, or a recent medication change—that started before these concentration problems got worse?

Um… I don’t think so? Nothing obvious comes to mind. I haven’t had, like, some big event where everything changed after it. I’m trying to think, because in nursing you hear “rule out medical causes” and then my brain starts making a whole checklist, but… yeah, I don’t have a clear answer like that.

I mean, I’ve had normal life stuff, being tired, stress, all of that, but I don’t know of any head injury or something neurological that lines up with when this got worse. No sudden “after this medication” thing that I can point to. I might be missing something, but nothing I’ve noticed.
Did these concentration problems get much worse after a specific traumatic or highly stressful event?

I don’t think there was one specific event like that. I’m trying to scan back through it, and there have definitely been stressful periods—work can be a lot, and life stuff kind of piles up—but I can’t point to one trauma or one big stressful thing where afterward my concentration suddenly got much worse.

It feels more like… it’s been there, and then sometimes stress makes it more obvious, if that makes sense. But not like a clear before-and-after from one event.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on a task all the way through, even when you’re not feeling especially stressed or down?

Yeah… definitely. Even when I’m not upset or particularly stressed, if I know something is going to take sustained focus, I kind of avoid it.

Like if there’s a big chart review or auditing documentation across shifts, I’ll keep putting it off. I’ll suddenly find all these bedside tasks that “need” doing first, or I’ll go check on something, or reorganize supplies—actually, the supply room at work drives me crazy sometimes because it’s never stocked the same way, but that’s not really the point.

The point is, sitting down with that kind of focused paperwork feels like trying to climb a wall. I know I can do it, but getting through it all the way feels… almost physically hard.
Do you often make careless mistakes because you miss details?

Yeah… I do. And it’s frustrating because it’s not like I don’t know the details matter—especially at work, obviously they matter a lot.

I’ll think I finished an EHR audit or checked a transfer note, and then my supervisor will find something like I missed a required field, or I put the wrong time on a medication follow-up, or copied the wrong room number. And I swear I looked right at it. That’s the part that makes me feel kind of crazy, because I’ll remember looking at the screen, but somehow the detail just… didn’t register.

And then I overthink it afterward, like, “How did I miss that?” which is its own whole spiral. But yes, careless-looking mistakes from missing details happen more than I’d like.
Do you spend a lot of time feeling nervous or on edge?

Um… I’m not sure I’d say a lot of time. I mean, I get nervous like anyone does, especially if something important is coming up, but I don’t feel like I’m constantly on edge.

Although “on edge” is a little hard to define, because at work everything is kind of alert mode anyway—you’re listening for call lights, monitors, people needing things, someone asking you a question while you’re halfway through something else. So sometimes I come home and I’m still sort of… keyed up, but I don’t know if that’s nerves exactly or just leftover work brain.

So, I guess… no, not in a constant way. I haven’t really noticed myself feeling nervous all the time.
